description.value: Sasquatch Crossing Eco Lodge is an Indigenous-owned and operated historic property on 87 acres in Sts'ailes territory near Harrison Mills, BC. Originally constructed in 1903 as Fenn Lodge and acquired by the Sts'ailes First Nation in 2009, the lodge runs largely on creek-powered hydro-electric energy and offers seven uniquely themed guest rooms. Touring cyclists will find it a scenic base for the Harrison Valley with mountain biking, birding, and Harrison Hot Springs all within easy range.

address.value: 15500 Morris Valley Road, Harrison Mills, BC V0M 1A1

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website amenities page explicitly lists 'FREE WIFI' and confirms it in the amenities body text ('We also offer free Wi-Fi'). The amenities page mentions free parking but no bike storage, bike racks, or any cycling-specific infrastructure anywhere on the site. The Chehalis Store & Gas station is cited as a 3-minute drive with 'a great selection of delicious fresh food,' supporting a nearby grocery finding.
concerns: OSM community field lists 'Chilliwack' but the property's actual address is Harrison Mills, BC — approximately 30 km from Chilliwack proper.
No bike storage, bike handling procedures, or any cycling-specific amenities are mentioned anywhere on the website.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The lodge is a legitimate, active accommodation well-placed for touring cyclists in the Harrison Valley, but the website makes no mention of bike storage or any cycling-specific services, leaving the two required WWC criteria unconfirmed. Direct outreach to verify secure bike storage would resolve this.
enrichment_extras.notes: The lodge mentions mountain biking as one of the nearby activities, suggesting some cyclist clientele, but no dedicated cycling infrastructure is documented.
